panels.notes: [OUTLINE 1 · PREPARE LOGISTICS] Before going live: test audio and camera, open the chat, have your team ready to drop the link and welcome names. [Smile] Say nothing for three seconds, then read the line slowly. [PAUSE] This question is the heart of the Graduation Game, so it is also the heart of today. [2 min]

panels.label: Cameras on
panels.title: Cameras on. Write where you are from in the chat.
panels.notes: [OUTLINE 1 · LOGISTICS] Housekeeping in one breath: cameras on, say your city, mute when not speaking. Read three or four names aloud as they come in. Make them feel seen before you teach. [ROOM MOVE] Chat word: city name. [2 min]

panels.label: Three rules
panels.title: Three rules for today.

cards.title: Play along in the chat
cards.body: When I ask, you type. It keeps us all in the game.

cards.title: An offer is coming
cards.body: At the end I will share the next step. You decide.

panels.notes: [OUTLINE 1 · SEEDING] Rule three is the seed: tell them honestly that an offer comes at the end. Honesty now removes resistance later. [Smile] Ask: 'Is that okay with everyone? Write OK.' [ROOM MOVE] Chat word: OK. [2 min]

panels.label: The promise
panels.title: By the end, you will know your next step on the ==money ladder==.
panels.notes: [OUTLINE 2 · SEEDING] One line promise. Plant the ladder idea: Guest, Regular, VIP, Gold. Say: 'Every one of you is standing on one of those steps today.' Do not sell yet. [1 min]

panels.label: The problem
panels.title: Most people play to win a round. Few learn to change.
panels.notes: [OUTLINE 3 · PROBLEM] Tell it as a story: 'I have watched player after player do the same thing. Small deals, build capital, wait for the Big Deal, get out of the Rat Race. Then the Big Deals disappear.' [PAUSE] Ask: 'How many of you realise the rules of money are changing?' [ROOM MOVE] Chat word: ME. [3 min]

panels.label: Two ways to play
panels.title:
You can wait for the Big Deal.
Or you can ==learn to adapt==.
new: Change your play when the rules change
panels.notes: [OUTLINE 3 · SOLUTION] This is the solution in one picture. It comes straight from how the Graduation Game is facilitated: the Big Deal cards are removed and the player must discover another way. Guide, do not give away the answer. [3 min]

panels.label: The low point
panels.title: The Big Deal cards are gone. ==Now what?==
panels.sub: That moment is where players grow.
panels.notes: [PAUSE] [Lower your voice. Look into the camera.] Tell the emotional story in your own words: a real player you facilitated, the moment the Big Deals were removed, what they felt, what they changed. Use a real first name only with permission. NEED: replace this beat with your true story. [3 min]

panels.label: Value by comparison
panels.title: Value is measured by ==comparison==.
panels.notes: [Teach one win] Taken from the club's own assessment: a player must tell a good deal from a bad deal. Ask the room: 'Which is better, a deal that pays 8 percent or one that loses money?' Obvious? Good. Now make it harder on the next slide. [2 min]

panels.label: Good deal or bad deal
panels.title: A shopping mall at ==-24% ROI== is not a good Big Deal.
panels.notes: [Teach one win] The club's own example: the Shopping Mall can look like a Big Deal, yet at minus 24 percent ROI it is not a good one. Ask: 'Would you buy it?' [ROOM MOVE] Chat word: YES or NO. Reveal: size is not the measure, return is. [3 min]

panels.label: Your turn
panels.title: Write one deal you passed on. Was it really a bad deal?
panels.notes: [Watch, then do] Give them three minutes of silence. Then ask two or three people to share. Pattern interrupt: stand up, stretch, then continue. [3 min]

panels.label: The result
panels.title: You just practised the skill the ladder is built on.
panels.notes: Close the win: they now see value by comparison. Say: 'That is one skill. The club teaches many, one game at a time.' [1 min]

panels.label: Thank you
panels.title: Thank you for playing along.
panels.notes: [OUTLINE 5 · THANK YOU] Thank them sincerely, by naming two or three people who took part. Gratitude earns the right to ask. [Smile] [1 min]

panels.label: Permission
panels.ask: Would it be okay if I shared a small offer with you?
panels.notes: [OUTLINE 4 · ASK PERMISSION] Ask warmly, then wait. Read out every OK. Anyone who does not answer is not ready, and that is fine. [ROOM MOVE] Chat word: OK. [2 min]
